sources.name: lics2015
sources.title: A Canonical Form for Weighted Automata and Applications to Approximate Minimization
sources.proposition: For a finite alphabet and nonzero real-valued function on all finite strings, its Hankel matrix H(p,s)=f(ps) has finite algebraic rank n iff f has an exact real weighted finite-automaton realization with minimum state dimension n.
sources.boundary: Ordinary real addition/multiplication and equality on every string. No summability assumption for this algebraic theorem; later SVD/operator results impose extra assumptions. No minimum among nonnegative/stochastic or nonlinear realizations, no finite-sample learning or approximate-rank bound. The zero function requires a zero-state convention and is excluded from this import.
sources.location: Section II.B, PDF pp3-4, Theorem2; p3 defines rank(f) as minimum WFA dimension.
sources.identity: LICS2015 pp701-712, identity independently verified via Crossref and author bibliography. Classical result restated and attributed to Berstel-Reutenauer2011 [27], not an original theorem claim by these authors.

sources.name: fithian-sufficiency
sources.title: Sufficiency — legacy Statistics 210A lecture04 handout
sources.proposition: For a nonempty countable discrete sample space and nonempty family of everywhere-positive probability masses, a sufficient discrete statistic T is minimal sufficient if proportional likelihood functions imply equal T values.
sources.boundary: This is the countable positive-support specialization of the displayed sufficient-statistic criterion, with minimality among discrete statistics. Likelihood proportionality uses one positive constant independent of the parameter. The corresponding likelihood-class partition follows by factorization, not a separate displayed theorem. General dominated models require almost-everywhere and measurable-version qualifications; no pointwise continuous-model partition or identification with an arbitrary deterministic task quotient is inferred.
sources.location: PDF p7 minimal-sufficiency definition; p8 displayed Thm3.11, proof and locating quote; p4 dominated factorization.
sources.identity: Author-hosted legacy handout, exact publication date unverified. PDF metadata has a 2020 date; do not assign the separate Fall2023 version. Companion author page sufficiency.html is dated2023-08-29 and independently states the a.e. factorization qualification. Classical course restatement, not the original historical proof.
